_meta.indication: ORGOVYX is a GnRH receptor antagonist indicated for the treatment of adult patients with advanced prostate cancer.

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, randomized (2:1), open-label, parallel-group study comparing oral relugolix (360 mg loading dose Day 1 then 120 mg daily) to leuprolide acetate depot injection every 3 months over 48 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Men with androgen-sensitive advanced prostate cancer who required at least 1 year of continuous androgen deprivation therapy (ADT).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained castration rate: cumulative probability of testosterone suppression to < 50 ng/dL from Week 5 Day 1 (Day 29) through 48 weeks (success if lower bound of 95% CI >= 90%).
pivotal_trials.result: HERO met its primary endpoint: 96.7% (95% CI 94.9, 97.9) of relugolix patients achieved and maintained sustained castration (< 50 ng/dL) from Day 29 to Day 337, with lower CI bound exceeding 90%; leuprolide castration rate 88.8% (95% CI 84.6, 91.8).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) and laboratory abnormalities (>=15%): hot flush (54%), glucose increased (44%), triglycerides increased (35%), musculoskeletal pain (30%), hemoglobin decreased (28%), ALT increased (27%), fatigue (26%), AST increased (18%), constipation (12%), and diarrhea (12%).
target_moa: Oral GnRH antagonist that competitively blocks GnRH receptors in the anterior pituitary, preventing LH and FSH release and thereby suppressing testosterone production; androgens such as testosterone stimulate prostate cancer growth.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to an advisory committee.

summary.text: NDA 214621 for relugolix (ORGOVYX) received Priority review and was granted regular (full) approval based on the phase 3 HERO study, without accelerated approval, orphan, breakthrough, or fast track designations; the application was not presented to an advisory committee.

The recommendation for regular approval of this application for relugolix is based on efficacy and safety from the HERO study, a multinational, randomized, open-label, parallel-group study in patients with advanced androgen-sensitive prostate cancer who required at least 1 year of continuous androgen deprivation therapy (ADT).
This application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee.
